scope: Research-only normalized fields. Original extraction JSON files remain unchanged and are authoritative source documents.
taxon_policy: Original repository IDs unchanged; accepted names remain pending taxonomic review where flagged.
bonap_policy: No county assignment until direct species-map verification.

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Root-hemiparasitic herb, 40–80 cm (genus treatment)
characters.flowers: Pedicels to 30 mm, calyx lobes to 0.5 mm; pink/purple corolla 20–23 mm with two yellow throat lines and many small red-purple dots; source key short racemes 3–4 pairs of pedicels and internal narrow hair line below posterior sinus
characters.habitat: Thin limestone soils, Edwards Plateau

research_caveats: Source states Texas endemic; independent county-level BONAP verification pending

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Root-hemiparasitic herb 30–100 cm (genus treatment)
characters.leaves: Mostly narrow/linear, sometimes basally lobed (key)
characters.flowers: Pedicels 1–3 mm; calyx tube 3.5–5 mm with acute lobes; corolla 20–32 mm, deep pink to white/lavender tinged, two yellow lines and small dark-purple throat spots; key calyx lobes as long or longer than tube
characters.habitat: Prairies and open woodlands

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Much-branched shrub to 3 m; young twigs minutely pubescent
characters.leaves: Opposite green lanceolate/elliptic/narrow-oblong blades 3–27 × 2–8 mm, usually entire or 1–4 teeth each side; often smaller axillary leaf fascicles
characters.flowers: Sweet vanilla-scented flowers in peduncled upright dense spike-like racemes 2–7 cm; white or violet-tinged corolla with green-yellow eye, tube ca. 3.5 mm, limb 3.5 mm across
characters.habitat: Rocky or gravelly ground

research_caveats: Flora treats species broadly while describing morphological differences for varieties gratissima and schulziae.

https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/aloysia-virgata/

characters.growth_habit: Fast-growing arching woody shrub or small tree, horticultural 5–15 ft tall, long slender stems
characters.leaves: Opposite, ovate–elliptic, 4–9 × 1.5–6 cm; margins dentate, variable pubescence, green above and often paler beneath
characters.inflorescence: Lax, often flexuose axillary racemes, sometimes several per leaf axil; flowers small, white, strongly fragrant
characters.habitat: Native South American lowland scrub and disturbed habitats, not Texas-native
characters.flowering_period: July through frost in horticultural NC reference; not a universal native-range season

research_caveats: Kew notes great variability in tooth pattern, size, and hairiness of leaves; avoid over-specific field key.

source_references: Diggs et al. 1999

characters.growth_habit: Shrub to ca. 1.5 m
characters.leaves: Blades to 5 cm × 2 cm; petioles to 1 cm
characters.flowers: Single or paired in terminal one-sided spike-like inflorescences; calyx ca. 5 mm; reddish two-lipped corolla 30–40 mm, upper lip nearly entire, lower 3-lobed; 2 stamens
characters.habitat: Native Edwards Plateau; planted and sometimes escapes

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Mat-forming succulent glabrous wetland perennial (source genus)
characters.leaves: Opposite, sessile, spatulate, to ca. 20 mm, essentially entire; single prominent vein and wedge-shaped non-clasping base (key)
characters.flowers: Axillary single flower per node on stalks to 25 mm with two narrow bracts below calyx; white to pale blue or lilac corolla 8–10 mm; genus 4 stamens
characters.habitat: Low wet ground, ditches, streams

characters.growth_habit: High-climbing woody evergreen vine
characters.leaves: Usually two leaflets per leaf; disk-bearing branched tendril terminal, leaflet bases cordate, petiole 1–2 cm
characters.flowers: Axillary clusters; red-orange corolla lighter within, 4–5 cm long
characters.habitat: Moist woods, especially eastern Texas; cultivated and sometimes spreads or escapes in north-central Texas

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Slender scabrous-pilose root-hemiparasitic perennial to ca. 80 cm, usually unbranched erect stems
characters.leaves: Opposite/subopposite sessile elliptic-linear-lanceolate blades to 10 cm, entire to coarsely few-toothed, dark green blackening in drying, larger three-ribbed
characters.flowers: Terminal nearly leafless spikes, purple/violet/lavender-pink rarely white four-unequal-lobed corolla with tube 7–15 mm and lobes 3–8 mm
characters.habitat: Sandy soils, prairies, open woods, wet ground

research_caveats: No flowering time stated in individual 1999 treatment; leave null

source_references: https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=BURAR
https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:545866-1

characters.growth_habit: Perennial shrub; drooping stems to around five feet long in Wildflower Center treatment for subsp. racemosa
characters.flowers: White to yellow (subsp. racemosa Wildflower Center profile)
characters.habitat: Dry, shaded habitat in Wildflower Center profile; Kew reports native range Texas Edwards Plateau

research_caveats: Source subspecies racemosa only; species level can include other infraspecific taxa. Leaves and quantitative corolla characters held for primary FNA treatment.

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Soft-wooded, stellate-pubescent shrub 0.7–3 m with widely spreading branches
characters.leaves: Petioles to 38 mm; aromatic elliptic–ovate blades 8–23 cm long, sharply toothed
characters.flowers: Axillary cymes; small funnel-shaped 4-lobed corollas lavender-pink to bluish, reddish or white; corolla tube 2.6–2.9 mm
characters.fruit: Drupaceous, strongly clustered, rose-pink through violet/red-purple, globose 3–6 mm diameter, spicy odor
characters.habitat: Woods, especially low ground

research_caveats: Modern repository assigns Lamiaceae; historical source places this genus in Verbenaceae.

characters.growth_habit: Shrubby climber with aerial adventitious rootlets, to 10 m or more
characters.leaves: Odd-pinnately compound
characters.flowers: Terminal panicles; calyx teeth ca. 1/5 of tube; orange to orange-red corolla 2–2.5 cm with 5 short recurved lobes
characters.habitat: Stream banks, disturbed areas, fence lines, cultivation; eastern half of Texas

research_caveats: Use exact source corolla measurement despite potential discrepancy with other floras; later crosscheck explicitly.

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Hemiparasitic annual from slender taproot; pubescent (genus/key)
characters.leaves: Sessile/subsessile, mostly entire except lowermost; bracts entire or with small apical lobes
characters.flowers: Dense terminal bracted spike with usually orange-red to red showy bract/calyx tips; corolla 20–28 mm, upper hood 6–9 mm
characters.habitat: Sandy or silty open woods, prairies, disturbed sites

research_caveats: Flora describes rare light-yellow plants and reports natural hybridization/introgression with C. purpurea

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Root-hemiparasitic perennial with woody root (species group/key)
characters.leaves: Narrow, usually lobed (source genus key)
characters.flowers: Corollas 25–40 mm, hood 9–13 mm (C. purpurea group), bract/calyx tips yellowish orange, brownish-orange, orangish-red or red; lower lip typically 1.5–3(–4) mm (variety key)
characters.habitat: Calcareous gravelly, sandy or clay soils

research_caveats: CRITICAL crosswalk: repository species Castilleja lindheimeri versus 1999 C. purpurea var. lindheimeri. The flora calls it weakly differentiated and reports a sharp geographic transition; do not assume current rank without verification.

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Root-hemiparasitic perennial with woody root
characters.leaves: Narrow lobed leaves (source key)
characters.flowers: Variable colored floral bracts and calyx tips; corollas 25–40 mm, hood 9–13 mm; source distinguishes vars. citrina, lindheimeri, purpurea by tip color and lower corolla lip size
characters.habitat: Calcareous prairie, rocky or sandy sites depending on variety
characters.flowering_period: Mar–May in vars. lindheimeri/purpurea; Apr–May in var. citrina

research_caveats: Source is broad species covering three varieties; potential hybridization with C. indivisa and among varieties documented.

source_references: https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:30194969-2/general-information

characters.growth_habit: Tree to around 10 m with rounded crown, as described in Flora of Tropical East Africa
characters.leaves: Large simple ovate leaf blades 7–30 × 7–30 cm, truncate to somewhat cordate base
characters.flowers: White corolla with purple and yellow markings
characters.fruit: Narrow cylindrical ridged capsule up to 40 cm

research_caveats: 1999 local flora treats C. speciosa rather than this species. Measurements from separate Catalpa bignonioides treatment; no conflation.
records.source_status: treatment extracted; later cross-source morphology and BONAP county-level auditing pending

characters.growth_habit: Deciduous tree to 30 m
characters.leaves: Ovate to ovate-oblong blades 15–30 cm, truncate to cordate base and acuminate tip; petioles to 15 cm
characters.flowers: Few-flowered showy panicle; white corollas ca. 50 mm with yellow lines and brown-purple internal markings
characters.fruit: Cylindrical capsule 20–45(–60) cm long, about 1.5 cm thick
characters.seeds: Flat, 30–40 mm long and 4–5(–8) mm wide
characters.habitat: Cultivated, roadsides, streams; historical escapes east Texas

characters.growth_habit: Shrub or small tree to 10 m
characters.leaves: Opposite or alternate, narrow linear-lanceolate entire blades
characters.flowers: Terminal racemes to 30 cm; white/purple/yellow patterned corollas varying widely, some flowers sterile
characters.fruit: Capsules to 30 cm long, usually ca. 6 mm thick
characters.habitat: Cultivated highway and landscape plant, persists and sometimes escapes in north-central Texas; historically native farther west

source_references: Diggs et al. 1999

characters.growth_habit: Perennial herb to 0.7(–1) m
characters.leaves: Blades to 12(–15) × (1.5–)2–7 cm; petioles (0.5–)2–7+ cm
characters.flowers: Axillary short-peduncled to subsessile clusters, involucre of 2–4 floral bracts; obovate bracts to 7 × 2–5 mm; pink to purple (rare white) corollas 15–20 mm, upper lip entire or shallow 2-lobed, lower usually entire
characters.fruit: Stipitate ovoid emarginate capsule 5–6 mm; 2–4 seeds
characters.habitat: Moist wooded stream bottoms and wet habitats

source_references: Diggs et al. 1999

characters.growth_habit: Rhizomatous ± pubescent perennial; erect or partly decumbent stems 7–30 cm
characters.leaves: Sessile linear to oblanceolate obtuse blades
characters.flowers: Sessile axillary flowers shorter than leaves, foliaceous bracts; sepals united ca. 1/4, acuminate lobes 9–13 mm; lavender corolla with dark throat dots 15–27 mm
characters.habitat: Rocky or sandy ground

source_references: https://www.npsot.org/posts/native-plant/forestiera-angustifolia/
https://www.gardenstylesanantonio.com/plants/desert-olive/

characters.growth_habit: Densely branched shrub or small tree; stiff lateral branchlets commonly branch nearly at right angles, elbow-like
characters.leaves: Small narrow linear leaves in clusters along twigs; foliage variably semi-evergreen depending on region
characters.flowers: Inconspicuous separate male/female flowers on separate plants; early spring clusters before leaves
characters.habitat: Dry open sites, sandy well-drained soils and brush habitats
characters.flowering_period: Flowers usually January–April across referenced Texas sites

research_caveats: Older names Forestiera puberula and F. texana reported by NPSOT; synonym status requires POWO check; do not conflate F. pubescens

characters.growth_habit: Deciduous shrub with looping, sometimes half-vining stems
characters.leaves: Blades acute or obtuse, 2.5–4 cm, petioles 1–7 mm; glabrous in var. glabrifolia, pubescent in var. pubescens
characters.flowers: Sexes generally separate; flowers before leaves; female umbels/corymbs 3–12 flowers; filament 1–4 mm (source key)
characters.habitat: Limestone outcrops, pastures, brushy prairies

research_caveats: 1999 recognizes two varieties glabrifolia and pubescens; variety-specific pubescence must not be universalized.

characters.growth_habit: Small deciduous tree to ca. 16 m, glabrous
characters.leaves: Leaflets mostly 5 (range 5–7), often drooping, suborbicular-ovate to obovate or narrowly elliptic; key usually <6(–8) cm, 1.75–2.5× as long as wide
characters.flowers: Early spring, corollas absent as in genus
characters.fruit: Winged samaras 1.5–2.7(–3) cm, wing not decurrent on body (key)
characters.habitat: Limestone slopes and bluffs

research_caveats: Kew POWO and USDA GRIN synonymize Fraxinus texensis under accepted F. albicans; 1999 flora treats F. texensis distinct but allied to F. americana. Crosswalk evidence recorded, and separate identity confirmation for actual plants still needed.

source_references: https://texastreeid.tfs.tamu.edu/content/TreeDetails/?id=43

characters.growth_habit: Deciduous medium-sized tree to about 40 ft (12 m); broad dense rounded crown, drooping branches; trunk sometimes 2 ft (0.6 m) across
characters.stems: Gray to tan with narrow interwoven furrows/ridges
characters.leaves: Opposite, odd-pinnately compound leaves 6–10 in long, commonly five lanceolate leaflets, occasionally three or seven; leaflets 3–4 in, remotely toothed at least distally
characters.flowers: Dioecious; darker clustered male flowers often appear before leafout, loose female clusters with emerging leaves
characters.fruit: Tan slender samaras 1–1.5 in long, about 0.25 in wide
characters.habitat: Stream and river margins in South Texas; extensively planted elsewhere

research_caveats: Do not merge with F. pennsylvanica, historically problematic in ash complexes

source_references: https://apps.cals.arizona.edu/arboretum/taxon.aspx?id=391

characters.growth_habit: Small shrub-like, nearly evergreen tree commonly to 16–20 ft (5–6 m)
characters.leaves: Fine-textured dark-green pinnate foliage, individual compound leaves ca. 2 in long, lanceolate leaflets and fine marginal teeth according to University of Arizona arboretum
characters.flowers: Small petal-less clustered flowers in spring; typically dioecious
characters.habitat: Rocky limestone slopes, dry creek washes and canyons of southwest Texas and nearby Southwest

research_caveats: University source does not provide reliable samara dimensions; hold fruit measurements

characters.growth_habit: Deciduous tree to 20 m, usually glabrous in north-central Texas
characters.leaves: Opposite odd-pinnate with 5–7 leaflets; leaf bases decurrent, lateral petiolules 0–7 mm according to key
characters.flowers: Flowers in panicles before or with leaves, corolla absent; genus often dioecious
characters.fruit: Samara 3–7.5 cm, lanceolate to oblong-ovate; wing strongly decurrent along fruit body
characters.habitat: Stream-bottom woods and slopes

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Perennial, ascending stems densely hispid-hirsute
characters.leaves: Opposite, variable and 1–2 pinnatifid per flora key
characters.flowers: Bracts usually exceed calyces; calyx generally non-glandular pubescent or few glandular hairs; pink, lavender or purple salverform corolla; flora key tube usually 10–15 mm, limb 7–10(–15) mm; calyx 7–10 mm
characters.habitat: Disturbed areas, mainly western two-thirds of Texas
characters.flowering_period: Late Mar–Jun, less freely to Oct

research_caveats: Generic placement historically contrasted with Verbena using nutlets and chromosome numbers.

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Low annual with decumbent/spreading to erect stems, hirsute and often finely glandular
characters.leaves: Opposite, three-parted with incised divisions
characters.flowers: Spikes sessile or short-peduncled; pink to lavender or pale blue corolla, rarely white; key: corolla tube 8–10 mm, limb 3–5 mm across; calyx ca. 6 mm
characters.fruit: Genus 4 nutlets; key nutlet length 2–2.8 mm
characters.habitat: Sandy or gravelly soils

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Delicate ephemeral annual, 5–30 cm
characters.leaves: Basal leaves often purplish; petioles 1–4 mm; flora key gives ovate to elliptic 3.5–8 mm wide
characters.flowers: Calyx 5–6 mm, lower third of tube saccate; pink corolla 9–13 mm, not inflated; flora key notes corolla upper lip bent at right angle
characters.habitat: Rocky limestone soils

source_references: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon 1999, Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas

characters.growth_habit: Annual or robust perennial, 15–45 cm
characters.leaves: Usually essentially linear, 5–11 × 1–4 mm, entire
characters.flowers: Finely hirsute calyx 5–6 mm, tube saccate ca. 2/3; blue corolla 7–11 mm; key: peppermint aroma, strongly convergent upper/lower calyx teeth
characters.habitat: Disturbed habitats

research_caveats: Flora reports possible hybridization with H. reverchonii per Irving (1980)

characters.growth_habit: Aromatic low, basally much-branched plant, arching stems to approximately 10 in (25 cm) in southwestern field account
characters.leaves: Small ovate to roundish leaves ca. 1/3 inch (8 mm) long, entire and often with pointed tips
characters.flowers: Whorls above leafy lower stems; purple calyx with upper 3 lobes partly fused and lower two free; pink-purple two-lipped corolla with white patch on lower lip

research_caveats: Kew accepts H. nana and recognizes subspecies; field account may reflect southwestern populations, not all Texas plants. Do not equate subspecies nana and californica measurements.

characters.growth_habit: Woody-based robust perennial 15–60 cm; prior-season shoots persist
characters.leaves: Elliptic-oblong, 6–14 × 2.2–5 mm; gray-green in var. reverchonii
characters.flowers: Lemon-scented; calyx 6–7 mm; white or lavender corolla 10–15 mm with upward-expanded tube
characters.habitat: Open exposed calcareous outcrops

research_caveats: Do not automatically import characters of var. serpyllifolium into modern narrower H. reverchonii.

characters.growth_habit: Woody-based perennial; species group 15–60 cm
characters.leaves: Elliptic-oblong 6–14 × 2.2–5 mm in species treatment; dark green for var. serpyllifolium
characters.flowers: Camphor-scented; calyx 5–6 mm; mainly white, occasionally lavender corolla 8–10 mm, tube only slightly dilated
characters.habitat: Open exposed calcareous outcrops

research_caveats: POWO accepts Hedeoma serpyllifolia at species rank; ITIS accepts H. reverchonii var. serpyllifolia; retained source's narrower variety characters.

characters.fruit: Sessile glabrous narrowly oblong capsule 8–13 mm
characters.habitat: Wetland/riparian habitat reported by other authorities; not established from 1999 flora

characters.growth_habit: Glabrous rhizomatous colonial perennial; erect stems to ca. 100 cm
characters.leaves: Sessile or nearly so; narrowly oblong-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate
characters.flowers: Axillary peduncled dense spikes to 3 cm; peduncles to 15 cm; sepals linear-lanceolate ca. 7 mm, nearly free; white or violet corollas 10–12 mm with red-purple spots; genus treatment describes two stamens and 3-lobed lower lip

characters.growth_habit: Low suffrutescent perennial
characters.leaves: Subsessile, ovate to oval blades to 4 cm long
characters.flowers: Solitary axillary or short-peduncled, peduncle <=4 mm, no floral bracts; calyx bractlets to 2.5 mm; lavender, rose or white corolla to 28 mm, slender cylindrical elongated tube, upper lip entire or 2-lobed, much larger 3-lobed lower lip with white patch and purple basal spots; stamens inserted near corolla mouth

characters.growth_habit: Low pubescent annual; stems basal decumbent and ascending above, 10–45 cm (genus treatment)
characters.leaves: Petioled floral leaf-like bracts longer than wide, often reflexed; blades and bracts green often tinged purple; crenate rather than lobed

characters.fruit: Mericarps yellowish to olive-brown with white scaly mottling (genus treatment)

characters.growth_habit: Unarmed or sparsely armed shrub to 2 m

research_caveats: Flora uses broad L. camara; horticultural hybrid Lantana × strigocamara is separately inventoried and should not be automatically synonymized or conflated.

characters.growth_habit: Armed or unarmed shrub to 2 m
characters.leaves: Ovate to broadly ovate, upper surface strongly scabrous; coarse marginal teeth 2–5 mm (source key)
characters.flowers: Bractlets 4–9 × 1–2 mm, persistent, oblanceolate/spatulate (key); flowers yellow or orange changing red; corolla tube 7–10 mm, limb 5–9 mm wide

characters.habitat: Non-native ornamental escape associated with disturbed habitats and edges

characters.growth_habit: Low annual 10–15(–20) cm, unbranched to much branched
characters.leaves: Opposite petiolate blades triangular-ovate in outline, 1–3 cm long, pinnately to bipinnately parted
